report.source_text: On neurological examination his cranial nerves were intact, he had no obvious muscle wasting of his limbs and no tenderness or fasciculations, with normal sensations (touch, pain, temperature, proprioception and pressure). He had normal tone, power, reflexes of his upper limbs. In his lower limbs, he had power 4/5 with absent left leg reflexes and just elicitable right leg reflexes. He had bilateral equivocal plantar reflexes. Cerebellar signs were negative. He had a wide based ataxic gait and was objectively nervous about walking.

report.source_text: As per our local guidelines and the paediatric neurology consultation, this patient disability grade was static (2–3) and did not worsen during admission. Conversely, he Clinically improved gradually during hospital stay, hence intravenous immunoglobulin was not given.17 He was managed conservatively, monitoring active symptoms as well as peak flow to ensure no respiratory involvement. His peak flows remained normal throughout admission (ranging from 210 to 240). He had ongoing back and leg pain, for which he was successfully treated for using analgesics along with an increasing dose of gabapentin 10 mg/kg once a day on day 1, 10 mg/ kg two times per day a day on day 2, 10 mg/kg three times per day on day 3 and then stopped. He obtained regular physiotherapy in order to regain skills and to avoid any muscle wasting.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 9-year-old boy presented with a 3-week history of worsening back pain, unsteadiness, and lower limb weakness. Neurological examination revealed lower limb power of 4/5 with absent to diminished reflexes, wide-based ataxic gait, and normal sensation and cranial nerves. CSF analysis demonstrated albuminocytological dissociation. MRI of the brain and spine showed symmetrical enhancement of the cauda equina nerve roots and proximal mastoid segments of facial nerves. Plain spine X-ray was normal. During hospitalization, his disability grade remained stable with gradual clinical improvement without needing IVIG treatment. He received symptomatic treatment with analgesics and gabapentin and underwent physiotherapy with stable respiratory function.
